verdict.rationale: Nix's own docs promise reproducible development environments, portability across machines ('if a package works on one machine, it will also work on another'), and builds that only see explicitly declared dependencies. Community reports add that reproducible builds produce identical binaries. However, the pack never documents a lockfile or the pinning mechanism that would guarantee identical resolved versions; flakes are mentioned only as a create-and-build workflow. missing for 10: documented lockfile mechanism (e.g. flake lock pinning of inputs), explicit docs on installing from a lockfile to get identical resolved versions, hands-on corroboration of cross-machine version identity for dev dependencies

support.subject: As a developer, I can install dependencies from a lockfile and get the exact same resolved versions on every machine

citations.quote: if a package works on one machine, it will also work on another.
Easy transfer of software environments between computers.
Under Nix, a build process will only find resources that have been declared explicitly as dependencies.
Reproducible NixOS builds mean everyone building it gets the exact same binary
